body:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: elevated inference latency in us-west-2, autoscaler failed to spin up extra GPU nodes (policy: reserved-burst). Trigger: 5m sustained p95 > 450ms for /v1/generate.
Alex Chen: ack. jumping on it.
Alex Chen: any customer-facing pages yet?
Nia (CS Lead): seeing spike in error reports from two large tenants — one is seeing request timeouts. CS is patching customers.
Oncall Bot: Pager routed to Alex Chen (primary oncall). Incident channel created.
Sara Patel: ping — can we force a fallback to cpu-backed endpoints for non-latency-sensitive traffic?
Mike Rivera: curious if this is regional capacity or autoscaler logic. I see several GPU nodes in PG terminating (preemption events) around 1893500005.
Hana Iqbal: we're also seeing many short-lived VMs in the pool (spin up -> fail healthcheck). Could be an image or mount regression from the recent infra agent deploy.
Ops SRE: looking at node startup logs, kubelet failing due to mount timeouts to NFS proxy. suspect NFS saturations causing nodes to fail join, autoscaler stops because node addition keeps failing.
Alex Chen: temporary mitigation: increase retry window for current autoscaler and manually add warm GPU nodes from the spare pool. Can someone scale up the warm pool to +6?
Mike Rivera: on it. running command: \n```
cloudctl compute resize-nodegroup --name gpu-warm-usw2 --delta 6
```
Mike Rivera: command issued, nodes requested.
Sara Patel: while that runs, can we route lower-priority tenants to the cheaper CPU endpoints? config change is in router: `route_priority` map.
Alex Chen: @Sara please patch router with `route_priority[tier:standard] = cpu-fallback` and push as canary for 10%.
Sara Patel: will do. deploying traffic rule now.
Oncall Bot: Traffic rule change detected and applied as canary (10%). Monitoring.
Nia (CS Lead): notifying impacted accounts: NIA-ops and media-x. they'll be throttled to cpu endpoints for the time being. sending message template now. :email:
Hana Iqbal: warm pool nodes are stuck in `Provisioning` because cloud agent can't mount KMS keys for GPU AMI. getting 403 from KMS.
Mike Rivera: is the KMS policy we rolled last week relevant? I recall we tightened cross-account perms.
Alex Chen: that might be the regression. Ops SRE, can you temporarily relax KMS policy to let nodes launch? We need nodes online asap and then do a secure follow-up.
Ops SRE: changing KMS policy to allow cloud-agent role to decrypt for gpu-ami-launch. I'll notify sec.
Ops SRE: policy change applied. warm pool nodes started to join. healthchecks passing.
Oncall Bot: GPU capacity >= baseline after warm-pool joins. p95 latency returning toward SLO. Continue monitoring for 10m.
Sara Patel: can we keep the cpu-fallback rule at 10% but expand to 25% to reduce tail risk?
Alex Chen: hold — let's watch 5m. if p95 < 300ms then scale back.
Nia (CS Lead): any update on customer impact window and timeline so CS can close tickets?
Alex Chen: customers saw 18-36m of degraded service, start 1893500002 -> 1893500038 (approx). We'll confirm after full logs.
Hana Iqbal: root cause notes so far: KMS policy change + NFS proxy saturation + autoscaler insufficient retry/backoff. Multiple small failures cascaded.
Mike Rivera: evidence: node launch error logs: `KMS: AccessDenied for kms:Decrypt` around 1893500006, and kubelet NFS mount timeouts at 1893500008.
Alex Chen: good work. plan for immediate follow-ups: 1) revert tightened KMS cross-account rule until formal rollout (Owner: Ops SRE, ETA: 2024-10-03 18:00 UTC) 2) add autoscaler retry/backoff config and circuit breaker for node provisioning (Owner: Mike Rivera, ETA: 2024-10-04 12:00 UTC) 3) increase NFS proxy capacity + add rate-limiting (Owner: Hana Iqbal, ETA: 2024-10-05 00:00 UTC) 4) create traffic fallback playbook for CS > automatic cpu-fallback rule (Owner: Sara Patel, ETA: 2024-10-03 20:00 UTC) 5) run post-incident full postmortem and schedule blameless review (Owner: Alex Chen, ETA: schedule by 2024-10-06)
Sara Patel: adding a quick mitigation: a router feature flag `cpu_fallback_auto` to enable automatic expansion during any region p95>400ms. I'll draft the flag and tests.
Nia (CS Lead): CS action: send consolidated incident note to impacted accounts with ETA, and follow up when postmortem is done. I'll own the outreach.
Ops SRE: creating remediation tracking ticket: INFRA-9243, adding the owners and ETA.
Alex Chen: I want a checklist for oncall: when autoscaler errors appear, run `cloudctl nodegroup describe`, check KMS decrypt logs, escalate to sec if KMS denies. Add to runbook. (Owner: Alex Chen, ETA: 2024-10-04 09:00 UTC)
Hana Iqbal: also recommend we add a synthetic probe that validates node boot path including KMS decrypt and NFS mount for a new node type. (Owner: Hana Iqbal, ETA: 2024-10-07)
Mike Rivera: I'll follow up with cloud partner on their KMS cross-account change window and ask for an exception process. (Owner: Mike Rivera, ETA: 2024-10-04)
Oncall Bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Escalation cleared at 1893500115.
Alex Chen: thanks team. schedule postmortem: propose 2024-10-08 16:00 UTC. I'll send calendar invite.
Nia (CS Lead): please include summary and P1 customer list in the invite.
Sara Patel: action: I'll prepare a short runbook PR for cpu-fallback and leave the canary at 10% until automated flag is in. PR link: https://git.redwood/internal/router/PR/4123 (will update)
Ops SRE: INFRA-9243 updated with full incident timeline, logs, and owners. Linking related infra tasks.
Mike Rivera: quick note — we should also consider an autoscaler metric for `node_launch_fail_rate` so we can alert earlier. Adding to backlog.
Hana Iqbal: logging: put `cloud-agent` verbose logs behind a transient flag so we can capture future boot issues without noise. (Owner: Hana Iqbal, ETA: 2024-10-06)
Alex Chen: closing tasks for the page: warm-pool scale and cpu-fallback applied, KMS policy temporarily relaxed, monitoring confirms SLO recovery. We'll track long-term fixes in INFRA-9243 and get a postmortem. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Nia (CS Lead): I'll update customers and close immediate tickets; will escalate if they want credits.
Oncall Bot: Thread archived for follow-up actions.
